chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who sold a sale which was not with him to a specified term, and guaranteed the sale. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

key_terms.لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ: not with him / not in possession

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods you do not currently possess?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of selling non-existent or unpossessed goods (bay' al-ma'mul) when accompanied by a guarantee (daman), a concept foundational to later Shia jurisprudence on deferred sales. It highlights the Imam’s (peace be upon him) pragmatic approach to commercial transactions, distinguishing this specific guaranteed sale from general prohibitions against selling what one does not own. The ruling underscores the importance of certainty and risk mitigation in Islamic trade agreements.
